text:
acme_netops: Hey team — since yesterday our apps started getting SSL handshake failures to api.redwood.com when routed through our corp proxy. Public internet calls work fine. Error from app logs: "TLS handshake error: alert handshake_failure (40)". Any ideas?

sarah_support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl/openssl) and confirm whether the proxy is doing TLS interception (mitm) or just TCP pass-through? :thinking:

acme_netops: We don't intercept certs — proxy is allowed to MITM some hosts but not this one. Quick test from a client behind the proxy: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/models --header 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.com/v1/models
*   Trying 54.210.XX.XX:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.com (54.210.XX.XX) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using UNKNOWN_CIPHER
* SSL connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* SSL: SSL-Session:
*    Protocol  : TLSv1.2
*    Cipher    : 00
*    Session-ID: 
*    Session-ID-ctx: 
*    Master-Key: 
*    Key-Arg   : None
*    Start Time: 1670000000
*    SSL-Session: TLSv1.2, cipher suite (0x0000)
* SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood.com:443 
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL_connect returned=35 errno=0 
```
We also tried openssl: 
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -servername api.redwood.com -tls1_2
CONNECTED(00000003)
403580:error:14077438:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:tlsv1 alert handshake failure:s3_pkt.c:1476:SSL alert number 40
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

sarah_support: Thanks. That looks like a cipher mismatch/handshake failure rather than cert verification. I'll pull in infra/ssl.

jim_eng_infra: Looking into it — can you confirm whether the corp proxy is doing TLS termination and re-issuing certs? If so, what ciphers are enabled on that proxy appliance? Many enterprise proxies disable ECDHE curves or only allow RSA key exchange which can break connections to our endpoints when we present an ECDSA cert and only support ECDHE.

acme_netops: Confirmed proxy is terminating TLS for outbound and re-signing with company cert. Netops says they recently hardened the cipher list to remove some ECDHE curves for policy. They provided this list: 
```
TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA
TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA
TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA
```
They said ECDHE was disabled for legacy client compatibility.

nina_security: That's the issue. Our public edge uses ECDSA certs and prefers ECDHE (X25519, P-256) + TLS1.3. If the proxy only supports RSA key exchange ciphers, the proxy cannot complete a forward-secure handshake with our server because there's no RSA key on our cert to do RSA key exchange. The proxy then fails the handshake (alert 40).

jim_eng_infra: To confirm from our side I ran a quick probe: 
```
# from our monitoring hosts
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -servername api.redwood.com -tls1_3 2>&1 | sed -n '1,40p'
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.redwood.com
   i:/CN=Redwood Inference ECDSA CA
---
Server Temp Key: X25519, 253 bits
---
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
---
```
So our edge only offers ECDHE/TLS1.3 + ECDHE-TLS1.2 ciphers for ECDSA certs. No RSA-key-exchange ciphers are available.

acme_netops: So is the fix on our side then? Netops is reluctant to re-enable ECDHE due to policy. Could we offer an alternative endpoint with RSA certs or older ciphers?

sarah_support: I can escalate this as an enterprise compatibility request. Two immediate options: 
1) Netops change: enable ECDHE curves (X25519, P-256) on the proxy for outbound to our endpoints (recommended).
2) Redwood option: provide a compatibility endpoint that supports TLS with RSA key exchange or an alternate TLS profile (not ideal due to downgrade in forward secrecy).

jim_eng_infra: For now we can offer a temporary workaround: if customers can route their calls through a passthrough egress (bypassing TLS termination) or use a NAT/VPC egress that doesn't MITM TLS, that will work. Long term we shouldn't weaken server-side crypto. I'll log an internal ticket to evaluate providing an alternate compatibility endpoint only for large enterprise customers who can't change proxy config.

nina_security: Additional troubleshooting steps for customer netops: 
- Run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -servername api.redwood.com -cipher 'ECDHE'` from behind the proxy to see if proxy negotiates ECDHE at all.
- Tcpdump from a host behind the proxy to capture ClientHello and check cipher_suites/SNI. Example: `sudo tcpdump -i any -s0 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap host api.redwood.com and port 443` then inspect in Wireshark for TLS ClientHello details.
- If proxy replaces cert, export the re-signed cert chain and check whether it's ECDSA or RSA. If RSA re-signed cert + proxy removed ECDHE, handshake may still succeed if server advertises RSA key-exchange ciphers (we don't).

acme_netops: I'll send the tcpdump to you and our proxy config. Netops says they can flip on ECDHE for a small set of hosts. Can you provide the exact hostnames and preferred curves?

jim_eng_infra: Provide these: `api.redwood.com` and `*.api.redwood.com` (for now). Preferred curves: X25519, secp256r1 (P-256). Prefer TLS1.3 support. If they need specific TLS1.2 cipher strings for legacy proxies, suggest: `ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384` then RSA fallbacks if absolutely required.

sarah_support: Action items: 
- acme_netops to send tcpdump + proxy cipher list and confirm whether proxy is re-signing certs (by end of day).
- jim_eng_infra to open internal ticket (INF-3242) to evaluate compatibility endpoint and attach cipher list from our edge.
- nina_security to draft short guidance doc for enterprise netops on recommended cipher suites and why ECDHE/ECDSA is required (security rationale).

acme_netops: Thanks — we'll try flipping ECDHE on their proxy for `*.api.redwood.com` and report back. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Incident 2026-02-23-18220 created: INF-3242 - evaluate RSA-compat endpoint for enterprise proxies (owner: jim_eng_infra).

jim_eng_infra: If we don't hear back in 24 hours I'll follow up with a short config snippet customers can hand to their netops.

sarah_support: Marking this thread tracked on our side. Feel free to @sarah_support when you have the tcpdump.

acme_netops: Will do. Thanks everyone.
